title: Fppf testing of representable morphism properties
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ a morphism of algebraic stacks over $S$ representable by algebraic spaces. Let $q:V\to\mathcal Y$ be a representable surjective flat locally finitely presented morphism from an algebraic space, and put $X_V=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$. Each of the properties flat, locally of finite presentation, etale, and open immersion holds for $f$ if and only if it holds for $X_V\to V$, independently for each property. The same assertion holds for morphisms of algebraic spaces. Furthermore, for a morphism of algebraic spaces $g:X\to Y$, if $V\to Y$ and $W\to X\times_YV$ are surjective flat locally finitely presented covers, then $g$ is flat (respectively locally of finite presentation) if and only if $W\to V$ is flat (respectively locally of finite presentation). Flatness and local finite presentation are therefore local on both source and target for these covers; no source-local assertion for etaleness or open immersions is made. The properties use [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-open-immersion] on scheme charts, and surjectivity means lifting field-valued points after field extension. An algebraic stack means a stack in groupoids with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a smooth surjective scheme atlas; stack, 2-fibre products and representability use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Properties of representable maps are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts. Surjectivity means that every field-valued target object lifts after a field extension.

proof.text: Put $B=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$. It is an algebraic space by [lem-sfb-representable-pullback-over-space]. For flatness, local finite presentation and etaleness, the forward implication follows from base-change stability in [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. For open immersions use their scheme-test meaning: for every scheme $T\to V$, $B\times_VT\simeq\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}T$ over $T$, so the required open immersion is one of the tests for $f$. This also shows base-change stability of open immersions in the representable sense, without assuming that $\mathcal X$ or $V$ is a scheme. For the converse fix an arbitrary scheme $T\to\mathcal Y$. Write $Z=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}T$ and $A=V\times_{\mathcal Y}T$. Both are algebraic spaces, again by representable pullback, and $A\to T$ is flat, locally of finite presentation and surjective by the chartwise calculus. There is a canonical equivalence $Z\times_TA\simeq B\times_VA$ over $A$: both parametrise an $\mathcal X$-object, a $V$-object and their identifications with the given $\mathcal Y$-object from $T$. This is the associativity universal property of the 2-fibre product.

source.place: Tag 04XD, lemma-check-property-covering, its two cartesian squares

proof.text: We will use the following elementary conversion whenever a surjective flat locally finitely presented scheme map $u:U\to T$ occurs below. The singleton $\{u\}$ is an fppf covering. For every affine open $T_0\subset T$, base change gives an fppf covering of $T_0$ by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change]. Apply [lem-pc-fppf-affine-refinement] to choose finitely many affine opens in $U\times_TT_0$ whose images cover $T_0$. These are affine opens of $U$, since $U\times_TT_0$ is the inverse image open of $T_0$. Together with flatness of $u$, this is exactly [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Hence $\{u\}$ is an fpqc covering in the family sense needed by the descent lemmas; $u$ itself need not be quasi-compact.

Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $U\to A$, which exists by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The composite $u:U\to A\to T$ is a surjective flat locally finitely presented morphism of schemes: etale maps are smooth, smooth maps are flat and locally of finite presentation, and these properties and surjectivity compose by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Thus Step 2 makes $\{u\}$ an fpqc covering. Fix one of the four properties $P$ and suppose $B\to V$ has $P$. Then $Z_U=Z\times_TU\to U$ has $P$: for the first three properties use base-change stability and $Z_U\simeq B\times_VU$; for open immersion this is directly the scheme test $U\to V$ of $B\to V$. These identifications respect projection to $U$. In particular, in the open-immersion case $Z_U$ is a scheme, rather than merely an algebraic space.

source.place: Tag 04XD, lemma-check-property-covering, refining the algebraic-space cover by an etale scheme atlas

proof.text: Suppose first $P$ is flat, locally of finite presentation, or etale. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $E\to Z$. Its base change $E_U=E\times_TU\to Z_U$ is a surjective etale scheme atlas by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. By [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties], $P$ is etale local on source-and-target, so [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion], with target chart $\operatorname{id}_U$, gives $P(E_U\to U)$. Now apply, respectively, [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-flat], [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-locally-finite-presentation], or [lem-galois-fpqc-descend-etale] to the scheme map $E\to T$ and the fpqc covering $\{U\to T\}$ from Step 2. This gives $P(E\to T)$. The same presentation criterion with source chart $E\to Z$ and target chart $\operatorname{id}_T$ gives $P(Z\to T)$. The argument handles each $P$ separately and uses no flatness hypothesis on $E\to T$ in the other cases.

source.place: Tags 041W, 041T, 042B: lemma-descending-property-flat, lemma-descending-property-locally-finite-presentation, lemma-descending-property-etale; their fixed-source-atlas arguments

proof.text: If $P$ is open immersion, Step 3 gives a scheme $Z_U$ and an open immersion $Z_U\to U$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-fpqc-open-immersion-descent] to the algebraic-space morphism $Z\to T$ and the fpqc scheme covering $\{U\to T\}$. It identifies $Z$ with an open subscheme of $T$. Thus all four cases give $P(Z\to T)$ for every scheme $T\to\mathcal Y$, which is precisely $P(f)$ by the defining scheme-base-change test. The same proof applies with $\mathcal X=X$, $\mathcal Y=Y$ algebraic spaces: their discrete fibred groupoids have the same fibre products, and the chart criterion identifies the scheme tests with the space properties for the first three cases; open immersion already has that scheme-test meaning. Consequently the stated target-local equivalences also hold for algebraic spaces.

source.place: Tag 041X, lemma-descending-property-open-immersion; stacks-properties.tex Tag 04XD, final scheme tests

proof.text: For the final assertion put $X_0=X\times_YV$ and $h:W\to X_0$. Write $P$ for flatness or, separately, local finite presentation. If $g$ has $P$, base change gives $P(X_0\to V)$, and composition with $h$, which has both flatness and local finite presentation by hypothesis, gives $P(W\to V)$. This uses the corresponding base-change and composition assertions of [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. For the reverse implication assume only $P(W\to V)$. We will descend through $h$ using scheme source descent and then use the target-local equivalence already proved with the given cover $V\to Y$.

source.place: Tags 06ET and 06EV, source locality; forward direction by composition

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale scheme chart $T\to V$, a surjective etale scheme chart $E\to X_T=X_0\times_VT$, and a surjective etale scheme chart $D\to W_E=W\times_{X_0}E$. These spaces and pulled-back etale covers exist by [def-trf-algebraic-space] and [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The map $D\to E$ is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation: $W_E\to E$ is the base change of $h$, and $D\to W_E$ is etale. Apply base change, composition and the etale/smooth implications of [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. On the other hand $D\to W_T=W\times_VT$ is etale: it is $D\to W_E\to W_T$, whose second map is the base change of $E\to X_T$. The base-change and composition assertions for chartwise etale morphisms in [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] justify this also for a possibly non-schematic $W_T$. Since $P(W_T\to T)$ follows by base change from $P(W\to V)$, the presentation criterion gives $P(D\to T)$, using the source chart $D\to W_T$ and target chart $\operatorname{id}_T$. Its source need not be surjective: the criterion asserts $P$ for every presentation once the space map has $P$.

source.place: Tags 06ET and 06EV, lemma-transfer-from-schemes expanded by scheme charts

proof.text: The scheme maps $D\xrightarrow{v}E\xrightarrow{a}T$ satisfy $av=D\to T$. If $P$ is flat, [lem-pc-flat-source-descent] applies because $v$ is flat and surjective and $av$ is flat, and gives flatness of $a$. If $P$ is local finite presentation, apply [lem-trf-lfp-fppf-source-locality] to $a$ and the singleton covering $\{v\}$: $v$ is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation, and $av$ is locally of finite presentation, so $a$ is too. Apply [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion], using [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties], first to $X_T\to T$ with charts $E$ and $T$, and then to $X_0\to V$ with the presentation $E\to T$. In the second application $E\to X_0$ is surjective etale, being the composite of $E\to X_T$ and the base change of $T\to V$, by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. Thus $X_0\to V$ has $P$. The target-local equivalence of Step 5 gives $P(g)$. Neither source-descent theorem requires quasi-compactness; no assertion about source locality of etaleness or open immersion has been used.
